Nerd News

Saturday, October 31, 2026 · last 7 days · updated 6:02 AM

Today's edition leans on rare-earth supply stress and defense AM funding, with a good set of event-camera and spatiotemporal monitoring papers for your LPBF work. On the magnetism side, the picks are DFT-plus-Monte-Carlo and symmetry tools that touch your T_C and anisotropy pipeline. In theory, there's kinetic Ising dynamics, a spin-chain realization, and a few big-picture ideas worth understanding.

Spatiotemporal graph transformer predicts metal AM build quality across layers

arXiv · AM monitoring & physics · 6/10

The abstract reports a transformer that fuses in-situ sensing, process settings and geometry to model multi-layer neighborhood interactions on build quality. This bears on your question of how temporal and cross-layer information changes predictive power. Check how quality labels were defined and whether the split is per-build or random.

Event-to-video reconstruction with a frequency-enhanced spatio-temporal network

arXiv · event-based vision · 6/10

The abstract describes a deep network that converts asynchronous event streams into video frames, adding frequency-domain processing to spatial methods. This likely maps onto the reconstruction side of your v2e/DVS evaluation on NIST data. Check whether it was tested on real event data or only emulated, and on anything resembling melt-pool brightness ranges.

DFT plus Monte Carlo on compensated ferrimagnet Mn3Al's finite-temperature magnetism

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

The abstract reports a systematic study of Heusler Mn3Al's electronic structure, finite-temperature magnetism and spin transport in tunnel junctions. The DFT-to-Monte-Carlo route resembles your T_C pipeline, though there is no Ce and no anisotropy focus. Check how exchange parameters were obtained and whether the T_C is compared with experiment.

Pentagon rare-earth deadline approaches; readiness in question

News · rare earths & magnets policy · 7/10

OilPrice.com frames an imminent Pentagon rare-earth deadline as a test of whether suppliers are ready. Only the headline is available, so the details are unconfirmed. Check which requirement applies and the date, since that decides how much the magnet supply chain you're motivated by is under pressure.

Nikon AM wins Department of War contract for Tomahawk mid-body LPBF systems

3D Printing Industry · 6/10

3D Printing Industry reports a contract for customized Nikon SLM Solutions LPBF systems, aimed at Tomahawk missile mid-bodies. It's a concrete sign of defense demand for larger LPBF machines, which should raise the need for qualification and monitoring. The snippet says nothing about in-situ monitoring, so check whether it does.

ML · Magnetic Materials

PythMPG code screens which tensors magnetic point groups allow

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

The abstract presents a self-contained tool, inspired by Bilbao's MTENSOR, that finds which tensors are symmetry-allowed per magnetic point group. This could help you constrain allowed anisotropy and exchange tensors for candidate structures. Check whether it handles the group assignments your CIF-derived lattices need.

DFT plus Monte Carlo on doping-driven magnetic order in Eu1-xGdxCd2P2

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

The abstract reports an exploration of Gd substitution effects on magnetic transition and magnetoresistance in a f-electron compound. It is a useful comparison for ground-state and order prediction, but it has no anisotropy focus. Check how it treats the f-electron correlation.

Compressed magnetic Moment Tensor Potentials cut parameters 1.5–3x

arXiv · magnetism + ML · 6/10

The abstract reports lower-parameter magnetic ML potentials that match the original on Fe-Al and CrN magnetic, structural and vibrational properties. A technique worth borrowing for magnetic-order modeling. Check whether it holds up for strongly correlated or f-electron systems, which the abstract does not mention.

Spin-reorientation transition in HoFe1-xAlxO3 single crystals with magnetic vacancies

J. Magnetism & Magnetic Materials · 6/10

Judged from the title only; no abstract is available. A rare-earth spin-reorientation study on single crystals is close to your anisotropy gap. Check whether it reports directional magnetization that could serve as validation data.

Additive Manufacturing

Hyperspectral melt-pool monitoring predicts composition in steel-to-copper DED

Additive Manufacturing (journal) · 6/10

The abstract reports hyperspectral imaging of the melt pool, used to detect and quantify compositional variation in 316L-to-CuCrZr structures. It is useful sensor-selection context, though it targets composition, not defects. Check how composition ground truth was measured.

Event cameras reconstruct fragment trajectories despite detonation flash

arXiv · event-based vision · 6/10

The abstract describes event-camera trajectory reconstruction and measurement of fragment position, velocity and energy under severe flash and smoke. The bright, fast, occluded scene is analogous to spatter around a melt pool. Check what multi-camera calibration was needed and how accuracy was validated.

Agentic LLM framework for WAAM porosity detection from process and acoustic signals

arXiv · AM monitoring & physics · 6/10

The abstract describes agents built on welder signals and acoustic data to identify porosity. The summary says XCT-validated labels, which is good practice, but the LLM-agent framing deserves scrutiny and it's not LPBF. Check the split strategy and whether the LLM adds anything over the classifier alone.

Physics-informed self-supervised network classifies laser-weld penetration from few labels

arXiv · ML for manufacturing · 6/10

The abstract introduces SimPhysNet, which classifies full penetration from molten-pool images with limited labelled data. Label scarcity is your problem too, though this is welding rather than LPBF. Check how the physics enters and whether testing was cross-condition.

Theoretical Physics

Kinetic δ-Ising model: threshold flip rules and hysteresis

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 6/10

The abstract introduces a kinetic Ising ferromagnet where spin flips are accepted if the energy change is below a threshold, splitting parameter space into kinetic sectors. It proves when global spin-inversion symmetry survives in the dynamics. It's useful background for your Glauber and Kawasaki MC, though it has no materials link.

Organic molecular crystal realizes a landmark spin-chain model magnet

APS Physics · 8/10

APS Physics reports that researchers built a crystal from organic magnetic molecules to access the physics of a landmark model magnet. Model magnets matter because their exact solutions let you test theory against a real material. Details are thin, so check which spin-chain model it is.

Supercritical crossover lines aren't uniquely defined, even with Ising scaling

arXiv · spin models & criticality · 6/10

Past the liquid-gas critical point, no sharp transition separates liquid-like from gas-like fluid. Recent crossover lines were proposed to respect Ising critical scaling; the abstract demonstrates the requirements don't pick out unique lines. The lesson echoes finite-size scaling: pseudocritical points depend on your definition.

Quasi-phases: distinct regimes near terminating critical lines

arXiv · statistical mechanics · 6/10

Plainly: a line of continuous transitions can simply end, like water and vapour beyond their critical point. The authors argue the gapped regimes beside the endpoint can still count as distinct 'quasi-phases', with interface modes between them. It is 1D quantum theory, so it is a conceptual frontier item, not something for your pipeline.

Advanced Manufacturing covers the ANSI–America Makes effort on AM standards. America Makes is your SAML lab's institute and qualification is central to your monitoring framing. Details are unconfirmed beyond the headline, so check what roadmap or documents it points to.
